methods.label: Centers and a square diagonal
methods.explanation:
Joining the circle centers turns the tangencies into known distances.

[Figure 1](figures/2007_AMC_10A_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

Let the original square have side length \(s\), and label the four small-circle centers \(P,Q,R,S\) in order around the square. A radius to a tangent side is perpendicular to that side, so each small-circle center is one unit inward from both sides at its corner. Consequently, \(PQRS\) is a square of side \(s-2>0\), with the same center as the original square.

Let \(O\) be the center of the radius-2 circle. External tangency gives
\[
OP=OQ=OR=OS=1+2=3.
\]
Because \(O\) is equally distant from the endpoints of each side of \(PQRS\), it lies on their perpendicular bisectors. Two adjacent perpendicular bisectors meet at the square's center, so \(O\) is that center. Thus the diagonal \(PR\) passes through \(O\), and \(PR=3+3=6\).

By the Pythagorean theorem applied to the center square,
\[
(s-2)^2+(s-2)^2=6^2.
\]
Since \(s-2>0\), this gives \(s-2=3\sqrt2\). Therefore the requested area is
\[
s^2=(2+3\sqrt2)^2
=4+12\sqrt2+18
=\boxed{22+12\sqrt2}.
\]
The answer is choice B.
